_note: HAND-AUTHORED campaign notes. This file is NOT generated and is never touched by tools/fetch-aon.mjs. Edit it directly, or edit session notes in the app (those live in localStorage, not here).
title: Mists of Zalazar

current.note: Next session: short Amber Hall RP, six months of downtime RP, the party reconvenes at the Pyramid where Amber warns them to BE READY FOR ANYTHING, then King Zalazar abruptly launches the first Wargames event: a two-week race from the Pyramid to Kir'gora.

arcs.title: Frontier Isle
arcs.summary: Landing at Port Suna, the escort to Woodfall, the goblin hunt, the march to Amberhall, and the Trials of the Sun King beneath the collapsed cliff.
beats: Party lands at Port Suna, receives map and gear, escorts Lukas Brightheart and his wares to Woodfall.
Goblins besiege the caravan trying to steal the wares.
Forward Commander Hall and Mabra Cypherbloom ask the party to find the goblin leader behind the raids on supply ships.
Failure state: ambush by a Drow Fighter and a Lizardfolk Scout.
At the goblin camp the survivors retreat into a cave. Goblin writing: strange creatures assault our shores, protect the horn, do not let the three-toes in.
Overland march to Forward Camp Amberhall through nature obstacles. Wolves track them by day and attack at night.
The reanimated owlbears.
A glistening lake, SIGIL MARKED — it recurs until someone names it aloud, and each time the Jinkin has tampered with one of their items.
Ancient ruins where Zuni conducts occult experiments and mocks each PC in turn.
Arrival at Forward Camp Amberhall under Vanguard Commander Jericho Hall.
Bridge-building under kobold siege. Climb down the cliff, cross the river, climb back up; holes visible in the far cliff face.
A flamethrower alchemist assists during the kobold attack; the bridge support collapses the cliff and he is crushed.
Cave systems. A Gogiteth feeding on adventurers meets a Giant Aukashungi and the two fight when the party arrives.
The Trials of the Sun King, inscribed in an old Jotun dialect.
After the trials: a sealed room, two days, then survivors including Jericho and Lukas force the middle door. A tunnel to a hatch inside a goblin fort guarding the Horn.
The Horn of Zalazar is blown. A week-long siege follows. The mists disperse and the Alliance can sail into Zalazar.

Trials of the Sun King: First Trial — The Summoning Stone. 'A soldier must prove their power and versatility.' Struck three times, the stone summons a creature keyed to the damage types used: three different types summons a creature weak to all three; a repeated type makes it heavily resistant; a single type makes it immune or healed by that type.

Second Trial — Stratagem of Radiance. 'A soldier must prove their wisdom.' A chess board with no initiative; enemy pieces move like chess pieces and one PC moves per turn. Pawns: Weak Oaksteward Enforcer. Knights: Orc Brute. Bishops: Weak Ifrit Pyrochemist. Rooks: Orc Warrior. Queen: Weak Drow Priestess. King: Ogre Warrior.

Fourth Trial — Empathic Erudition. 'A soldier must be compassionate and resourceful.' A different motif — murals of neighbours helping one another. Three goblets on pedestals, one poisoned; a beggar statue and a haughty nobleman statue both hold out their hands.
There are two horns: one on Frontier Isle, one on the coast of the Isle of Zalazar.

arcs.title: Kilika
arcs.summary: The large fishing settlement where the Alliance makes landfall on the main continent, and the Hunter Trials.
beats: Kilika fishes more than it hunts — hunting in the jungle is punishing. 21 floors.
Hunter Trial 1: capture an Ankylodon (SUPER ELITE) using healing fruit as bait.
Hunter Trial 2: catch a Gleamfish.
Hunter Trial 3: convince Ba'vira to grant a Hag's Toenail.
Hunter Trial 4 (HARD MODE): take an egg from a Tyrannosaurus Imperator's lair.

The Hag's dream layers: Sleeping deepens your layer by 1. Dying raises you back by 1.
Reality (Layer 0): the Hag, corrupted by the Bloodless One.
Layer 1 — Blue Butterflies: a vision of the young Hag explains that Hag's Toenail is only the name of a flower, offered freely in exchange for help with her research, Dream Treatment.
Layer 2 — Red Butterflies: the supposed dream world. Players can do as they like but cannot sleep; after seven days they die.
Layer 3 — Green Butterflies: the void, where those fully consumed by the nightmare reside — currently the real Hag. 'Dying should've been an escape, why can't I die?'

arcs.title: Pyramid of Zalazar
arcs.summary: The 351-floor pyramid where most trolls live, the Unmasked conspiracy, and the search for the Eye.
beats: 351 floors, shifting walls and swerving staircases that everyone treats as normal.
A central grand elevator holds 25,000 across 25 mini-elevators of 1,000 each, reaching floor 291.

Floors 1–76 work. Floors 76–335 residential. Floors 336–350 the king's direct vassals. Floor 351 the king and his family — nobody knows the way in; maids are sense-deprived and guided by the Queen herself.
The king works with his advisors at the very top, reached by an elevator from floor 350.

The Unmasked: an underground group undermining Zalazar's authority, breaking in using magical face-copying masks. Administration officer Lo'paal is the de facto leader, but Zuni supplies the masks and is manipulating him.

Zalazar the continent: An isle of high magic — everyone knows at least low-level magic.
Atheistic; they revere spirits but no gods. The king is revered as a deity become man.
Kitsune are not seen, only heard of in old stories — from the Third, Eighth, Eighteenth and Twenty-Seventh kings.
The Prince is always hidden and has a doppelganger. The court believes the Prince is the boy on the 350th floor; the real Prince poses as a young advisor to the King.
The Sun King, like Femur, is an Exemplar who received his powers from a deity without realising it.
The Troupe From Beyond: a travelling circus Zuni headed before becoming royal jester; a hidden section spreads his influence and the Bloodless One's.

arcs.title: Bitania
arcs.summary: The fortress and overseers' camp moving goods out of the Undermine — quality falling, prices rising.
beats: Little more than a defensive fortress and overseers' camp transporting goods from the Undermine.
Goods arriving are poorer and costlier than they used to be.
Goblins fleeing the Undermine report that the new boss, Gazlow, has worsened their contracts since taking power.

arcs.title: The Undermine
arcs.summary: A capitalist's dream world under Big Boss Gazlow, who has turned the Anvil Fortress into his personal castle.
beats: Gazlow has taken the Anvil Fortress — once the Zalazari's main weapon factory — as his personal castle.
His mechs punish anyone who does not pay his exorbitant taxes.
Goblins, ratfolk, dire trolls and kobolds report dropped wages, paid leave cut to four hours a year, and annual bonuses cut from a 54th week to two extra days.
With no way to rouse the people against him, most work through it and some start businesses.

arcs.title: The Circus
arcs.summary: A genuine one-day festival waiting outside the mine, its cheerful attractions quietly conditioning visitors for transformation. The investigation leads through Lo'paal's music box to a Blood God shrine.
beats: Exit the mine: the fully erected Circus waits directly outside, almost inviting them in.
Free roam: choose 2–3 attractions; most of the festival and its staff are genuine.
Investigation: clues point to the central tent, Lo'paal's office and the music box.
Finale: enter the Blood God shrine, fight Lo'paal, then the creature he summons.
Exit: the new PC arrives with the missive; the Eye is first mentioned in Pre-Wargames.

Festival entrance — Lo'paal: NPC: Lo'paal, Ringmaster; charismatic, theatrical, fully aware, deflects serious questions with showmanship.
Do: enter from the mine, meet Lo'paal, choose 2–3 attractions.
Line: 'Everything here is free. The only cost is curiosity.'
Normal attractions: Acrobats and jugglers: skilled troll performers; genuine show.
Games: ring toss, strength test and target shooting; standard carnival play.
Food and animals: festival treats; trained, well-treated creatures.
Fortune tellers: some genuine seers, some theatrical charlatans.
Fire juggler: holds one PC's gaze too long, then continues normally.
Memory Palace Maze — Ki'kara: NPC: cryptic seer; profiles visitors, reports to Lo'paal, says 'The mirrors show only truth.'
Do: navigate mirrors; describe a reflection doing something the PC might want to do.
Signs: reflections lag; whispers between panels; exit interview asks what they learned.
Perception DC 28: whispers are real words. Perception DC 31: Ki'kara's questions follow a profiling pattern.
Garden of Growth — Di'tola: NPC: passionate researcher; completely unaware; proudly defensive of her methods.
Do: inspect impossible flowers, visibly growing vines and heartbeat mushrooms.
Nature DC 23: this growth is impossible even with normal magic.
Perception DC 28: seeds or spores attach themselves to visitors.
Sculptor's Workshop — Vol'tola: NPC: revolutionary artist; knows the clay has special properties, not the full conditioning purpose.
Do: watch living clay reshape; answer her questions about physical potential.
Signs: eyes and teeth form; spectators copy poses; tools look surgical.
Crafting or Occultism DC 28: final forms were not intended. Perception DC 31: spectators are unconsciously mimicking them.
Palate Palace — Ku'taal: NPC: enthusiastic host; unaware of the conditioning; subtly altered; dismisses concern as small thinking.
Do: enter the eating contest; describe increasingly wonderful and disturbing food.
Fortitude DC 23, three checks: each success allows another impossible helping; failure means full.
Medicine DC 28: winners' widened jaws and extra teeth are real physiological changes.
Central tent — Lo'paal's headquarters: Clues: odd staff meetings, special rehearsals, nervousness about the ornate music box.
Maintenance worker: innocent, practical; noticed Lo'paal ordering special modifications.
Find: attraction plans, readiness reports, expansion contracts and staff lists marked Full, Partial or Unaware.
Music box sequence: mirror, flower, clay figure, open mouth.
Performance, Occultism or Religion DC 23: open portal. Thievery DC 28: bypass it.
Blood God shrine — Lo'paal: Scene: rib-like poles, wet curtains, breathing organ pipes, person-sized music box.
Lo'paal: use level-6 Puppeteer; reskin puppets as miniature PCs.
Trigger: summon at end of round 2 or when Lo'paal reaches half HP; ritual completes even if he falls.
Line: 'Every circus needs a little mystery, don't you think?'
Summon — The Grand Marionette: Creature: level-10 Roper, reskinned as a fleshy marionette; aberration.
Stats: AC 29; HP 215; Reflex +15; fire weakness 10; 50-foot strands.
Four PCs: standard Roper. Five PCs: Elite Roper, level 11.
Total with Lo'paal: 150 XP for four PCs; 190 XP for five PCs; Severe either way.
After the fight: Take Lo'paal's documents; shrine folds into the music box.
Return to frightened, mostly innocent circus staff.
New PC arrives with the missive; continue to Pre-Wargames.

arcs.title: Pre-Wargames — Six Months of Downtime
arcs.summary: Six months after the Circus: character-focused downtime, deliberate contact with future Wargames rivals, then a reunion at the Pyramid immediately before the race.
beats: Session order: 1) short Amber Hall RP, 2) six months of downtime RP, 3) everyone reconvenes at the Pyramid and Amber warns them to 'BE READY FOR ANYTHING', 4) the race begins abruptly.

By the time everyone returns to the Pyramid, the full party has seen every important Wargames adversary and collectively has useful information on all twelve NPCs. The Royal Guard and Alliance have likewise seen, heard about, or interacted with the party.
Keep relationship depth asymmetric: some NPCs are friends or rivals, some were only briefly met, and some were only observed.

Queek: Spends five months spreading pro-ratfolk propaganda among the Zalazari; keeps month six free to see what the rest of the party does.
His rolls and time spent in each region create stronger or weaker anti-Zuni hotspots there for the later Reclamation arc.
Pyramid: meets Aegon. Also sees Jericho, Mithri and Poppy; Jericho has already heard plenty of the ratfolk pitch, while the others do not particularly care or understand why Queek is so invested.
Kilika: meets Kali. Sees Ti'shan and Zalazi without meeting Zalazi; sees Henza and To'reno, who do not initially look especially remarkable; has a brief conversation with Musta.
Also sees Tandrun and may briefly meet him.
Femur: Spends all six months in Kilika retraining most of his chosen feats.
Regularly meets Ti'shan and Zalazi. Ti'shan is less cocky, more mature and grounded; he is training Zalazi in melee combat while clearly going easy on her.
Zalazi is terrible at melee, extremely proud, the first daughter of the Zalazar lineage in over 30,000 years, and pleased she is not 'bound to the Pyramid like a dog'.
Meets Kali and spars with her once. Resolve the whole spar with a single roll; Kali has a +2 edge.
Notices To'reno training once or twice and learns that he is an absolute madlad with a bow.
Vulpia: Pilgrimage between Kilika and the Pyramid to learn about herself as both Kitsune and Sylph while practicing new Kinesis techniques.
Meets Henza and gets along with him extremely well.
Meets Mithri, who thinks Vulpia's tails are fluffy, thinks she is nice, and shares treats with her to become friends.
Briefly talks with Kali. She does not conveniently see the rest of the Wargames cast.

Research: Kitsune appear intermittently in old Zalazari history and seem unusually associated with planar travel; this points toward the Realms Beyond, an interplanetary transit demiplane threaded with portals that routes teleportation and planar travel to the correct destination.
Research: her Sylph heritage is an elemental Air inheritance layered onto her Kitsune lineage.
Training breakthrough: she learns to create Cold and real ice through Fire + Air Kinesis by using Air for moisture/pressure/shaping and Fire in reverse to remove heat. This is not Water Kinesis.
Do not reveal the full truth of Faunus, Aurae or the Feywild catastrophe yet.
Gummo: Full-sends the Undermine for the entire downtime.
Founds a goblin-led anti-goblin political movement meant to atone for Gazlow's crimes: a deeply self-loathing movement built around goblins policing goblins harder than anyone else.
Meets Tandrun only, and Tandrun's only meaningful pre-Games PC connection is Gummo.
Rhea: Spends roughly one or two months learning soapmaking, then sells homemade soap in markets around Zalazar, mostly in the Pyramid.
This is deliberately outside her usual Guardian skillset: she is spreading her wings.
Meets Mithri when Mithri mistakes Rhea's soap for candy.
Priscilla: Drifts between the Pyramid and Kilika, keeping up with what the other party members are doing.
Let her player personally choose which Wargames NPCs she approaches, questions or spends time with.
She receives the broadest social familiarity / RP benefit of the party rather than a pre-scripted fixed contact list.
Session checklist: Downtime RP for all six PCs.
Reconcile at the Pyramid; Amber: 'BE READY FOR ANYTHING.'

arcs.title: The Wargames Arc
arcs.summary: A multi-stage national spectacle: a two-week race from the Pyramid to Kir'gora, a surprise five-day cooking competition in pairs, then qualification and team formation for the final three-team wilderness skirmish.
beats: The Games begin at the top of the Pyramid near the King's Throne and are magically broadcast for all Zalazari trolls to behold.
Phase 1: approximately two weeks racing from the Pyramid to Kir'gora. Racers may split up, help one another, help rivals, or push ahead alone.
Royal Emissary Vol'tika secretly awards extra credit for heroism during the race. Competitors are not told this beforehand.

Phase 2 is revealed only after the race: teams of two have up to five days to hand a dish to the jury. Faster is better, more delicious and original is better; judge mainly by vibes, creativity and rolls rather than rigid scoring.
After Race + Cooking, the Top 9 contestants are guaranteed places in the final event. They must form three teams of six (18 total); the other nine slots may be filled by anyone.
Expected but not forced outcome: Party vs Royal Guard vs Alliance in the final skirmish.

race.title: Wargames — Race to Kir'gora
race.scope: Approximately two in-game weeks from the King's Throne at the Pyramid summit to Kir'gora. Racers can split, cooperate, help rivals, or race solo. The later cooking contest and skirmish are not revealed in advance.

legs.name: Pyramid Escape
legs.guidance: Start at the very top near the King's Throne. The normal route uses the Pyramid's portal and transport infrastructure down to ground level. The Royal Guard immediately demonstrates that creative traversal is legal by using magic and mobility to leap from the kilometers-high Pyramid toward the first checkpoint at its foot. Accept any justified route: portal, internal transit, stairs, exterior structures, climbing, mitigated falls, or mobility magic.

legs.name: Village Leg
legs.guidance: A woefully unprepared civilian village sits just outside the Pyramid, and racers charge straight through. Keep the chaos comedic, never cruel: markets, carts, livestock, laundry, alleys, homes, and local traffic become obstacles. The King will overly compensate residents afterward for race-related damage. Helping people can cost time; shortcuts or forcing a path can gain it.

legs.name: Dinosaur Plains
legs.guidance: Flat tracks cross open plains where raw movement speed matters. The huge competitor stampede agitates roaming dinosaurs. Treat dinosaurs and stampedes primarily as moving race hazards, not stand-and-fight encounters. Racers can evade, redirect, calm, outrun, exploit, or get caught in the chaos.

legs.name: Mountain Area
legs.guidance: A major route choice: go around the mountain on a longer, safer route, or climb and jump over its substantial vertical terrain. Henza uses Earth Kinesis to burrow through the mountain, creating a third route. Other racers may notice, follow, or exploit the tunnel as circumstances allow.

legs.name: Jungle Area
legs.guidance: The longest wilderness-feeling stretch: dense foliage, navigation pressure, survival hazards, and jungle monsters. Encounters usually pressure racers to keep moving rather than stop for standard combat. Racers can cross paths, help each other, shadow others, or split routes.

legs.name: Final Stretch
legs.guidance: A final paved road into Kir'gora. No special trick or puzzle: remaining speed, mobility resources, fatigue, conditions, and current race position matter. Scattered racers converge so the finish plays as a visible race rather than an abstract final roll.

checkpoints: Checkpoint 2: near the mountain to the west.
Final checkpoint: the gates of Kir'gora.
opening: King Zalazar: 'Thank you for coming. These Wargames will be broadcast magically for all trolls to behold.'

'The first part of the Games is a race. There are checkpoints for you to go through: the first is at the bottom of the Pyramid, the second is near the mountain to the west, the third as you enter the jungle, and the last is at the gates of Kir'gora.'
Immediately demonstrate the tone by having the Royal Guard use magic/mobility to jump from the kilometers-high Pyramid rather than taking the normal portal route.
hiddenJudging: Vol'tika, not the King, assesses the race.
Heroism secretly improves a racer's overall result: helping civilians, rescuing competitors, protecting others from stampedes or monsters, and similar acts.
Competitors do not know heroism is worth anything until after the race.

Rules: Each team has 20 tags, split among its 6 members however they choose, plus 1 flag.
Scoring: each enemy tag captured is 1 point; capturing an enemy flag is 12 points.
Flags are immovable once placed — no relocating your own base.
A dropped enemy flag automatically returns to its owner's base.
No elimination: a team that loses all tags and its flag stays in the game, only the running score matters.
A fixed timer is magically projected in the sky, visible to everyone at all times. Final scores are tallied at the buzzer.
Tag theft is handled in the moment — generally Thievery vs Reflex DC, GM adjudicating unusual approaches case by case.
Alliance: The Alliance are newly arrived from another continent, friendly with the Zalazari trolls. Warm but competitive with the party — rivals, not enemies.
Team strategies: Royal Guard: the Kineticist carries all 20 tags and hides away from the flag, fortified by terrain (stone walls, root barriers) — a near-untouchable point bank.
Royal Guard: Ti'shan and the Princess run as a roving dual-assault duo hunting stragglers, free to play aggressively because the banked points cannot be taken.
Royal Guard: a disciplined, almost coldly tactical plan — worth a thought as to who designed it.
Alliance: tags spread fairly evenly, leaning slightly toward Mithri as their most mobile member.
Alliance: 2 defence / 3 attack, but adaptive — likely the team most responsive to the actual state of play.

cooking.title: Wargames — Surprise Cooking Competition
cooking.reveal: Immediately after the race: 'Between now and five days from now, as a team of two, hand in a dish for the jury to eat. The faster the better, the more delicious the better.'
rules: Contestants form teams of two however they like; 'chef + hunter' is obvious but not mandatory.
They have at most five days to submit one dish.
Submission speed matters, but so do taste, originality, ingredient quality, creativity and the actual rolls.
Judge on vibes rather than a rigid numerical score.
There are many additional background competitors beyond the Party, Royal Guard and Alliance; most are there to make the event feel large and do not have a realistic chance of winning.
The cooking competition is not foreshadowed during the race. Any useful ingredients gathered beforehand must have been collected naturally for some other reason.

format: Combine the Race and Cooking performance into an overall Top 9.
All Top 9 must participate in the final skirmish.
The contestants then form exactly three teams of six, for 18 total competitors.
The remaining nine slots may be filled by anyone.
How teams form is up to the contestants. Party vs Royal Guard vs Alliance is heavily expected but not mandated if the table chooses otherwise.
qualification.partyInsertion: Insert the three best-performing PCs into the six-NPC placeholder ranking wherever their Race + hidden heroism + Cooking performance and rolls feel appropriate.

arcs.title: The Vanguard March
arcs.summary: An army marches against the necromantic forces invading the last bastion of the troll empire. The Eye fails, and Amber Hall dies.
beats: Lukas, Amber, Jared, Jericho, Ti'shan and many other NPCs march with the army. Many ambushes.
Jared dies, along with other NPCs. Jericho, Lukas and Ti'shan survive.
Amber Hall reaches Level 15 by this point and carves through undead with ease.
Amber clears a path so the crown princess can use the Eye against the Lich. The Eye has no effect — he made it, and he reclaims it.
Zalazar the Second kills Amber Hall and begins a resurrection ritual on her. She becomes a boss fight later.
The crown princess is also killed in the encounter.
Ti'shan's grief, and what he does in the moments after, defines who he has become.

arcs.title: The Pocketwatch Quest & Zalazar the Second
arcs.summary: Time travel through the Forgotten Lands to reach the phylactery — and the conversation with the Lich that recontextualises the whole campaign.
beats: The Pocketwatch turns back time by years for a few hours, with long recharge periods. It must be reimbued at an ancient altar.
Musta the Russari provides his compass to the Mist-cast Morass, where Zandalari lore reveals the artifact in a lost tower.

The undead hordes guarding the phylactery are too vast to fight through, so the party travels back thousands of years to cross the Forgotten Lands — the original vast western continent before it shrank.
The closer they get to Zalazar the Second, the further back they are sent.
At journey's end they witness the sacrifice in real time. He cannot see them, but he looks in their direction for a moment before completing it.

Eras: Early Era: Zalazar openly mourned as a hero. Necromancy is funerary reverence; the undead are honoured ancestors serving willingly.
Middle Era: political tension creeping in, new religious movements calling it unnatural, the Blood God cult quietly reframing the narrative.
Later Era: active persecution, history being rewritten, the word Zalazar becoming a curse rather than a name.
Recent Past: full erasure. The trolls no longer know why their continent shrank; the Eye is a curiosity rather than a sacrifice.
Meeting the Lich: 'Aah, you have come. Not even the Radiance could protect my mind from being corroded over time, it seems. Come. We have much to discuss.'
He knows what the party is and the moment in time they came from. Recognising them as the party his past self prepared for is what makes this a conversation rather than a fight.
He will tell them what the Blood God actually is and wants; why the Blessing of Radiance passed to the princess; the true history of his sacrifice; and what he has been holding on for.
He may know which party member is destined to become the Arbiter — saying so directly or simply looking at them is a choice for the moment.

arcs.title: The Feywild Arc
arcs.summary: Thrown through the corrupted gateway. Vulpia's parents, a defaced Naiad Queen, and the Glimmerlings.
beats: Ti'shan's flying kick sends the party through the corrupted gateway into the Feywild instead of the Blood God's realm.

Vulpia's parents, Faunus and Aurae, were tasked with building political ties to the Feywild and the Plane of Fire. Fire failed; the Feywild had hope. They tried to expedite it by creating a single plane where everyone could live in harmony, and it went catastrophically wrong.
A defaced Naiad Queen posing as Nyrissa captures the party and asks them to rescue her daughter Aurae from the evil Faunus.

In truth: Aurae's mother died in the incident where they also lost their daughter. Faunus continued hoping to bring them back; the creature he made and merged with is a monstrous thing the Feywild has banded together to contain. Dimari-diji locked him up to stop the rift energies leaking.
'The arrogance to think that he, a man born of one plane, could manifest and control them all...'
The party experiences seven years in the Material Plane; their subjective time in the Feywild differs. Zuni uses the absence to consolidate absolute power.

The Glimmerlings: A silly band of creatures celebrating all the races of the Material Plane, throwing a party every day for a single race and shapeshifting into it.
Every Glimmerling must find a creature on the Material Plane when they come of age and show their companions the race they found.
On the Material Plane they are colourblind, so they often shapeshift into the wrong colour combination — and always add horns because they think horns look cool.
The Rat King is a Glimmerling who never came back.

arcs.title: The Corrupted World (Post-Feywild)
arcs.summary: Seven years gone. Two immortal antagonists rule, the real prince leads a rebellion, and Ti'shan returns as something else.
beats: Seven years have passed. The landscape is malformed by the Blood God's flesh constructions.
Two immortals now rule: Zuni, the Bloodless One, eternal through cancerous corruption; and Zalazar the Second, eternal through necromancy, believed dead 24,000 years.
The real prince emerges from seven years in hiding as a rebellion leader.
Captain Morgan — the Alliance general the party once stopped from conquering Zalazar — has gone rogue, joining Zuni with his corrupted fleet and blocking reinforcements.

Ti'shan reappears as an emotional boss encounter: grotesque and misshapen, a Blood God construct wearing the shape of someone the party loved. Whether anything of him remains is discovered in the fight.
The Alliance arrives in zeppelins for the final assault on the pyramid.

arcs.title: The False Victory and True Horror
arcs.summary: Zuni falls — and it turns out his monsters were the only thing holding the undead back.
beats: After the long assault Zuni falls. 'I accomplished my goals long ago. I was just going for extras.'
Zuni's monsters had been holding back Zalazar the Second's undead hordes. With them gone the true threat pours in, blocking every path to the phylactery.
The prince, empowered by seven years in hiding, ascends to the throne with new abilities and holds off the undead long enough for the party to act.

arcs.title: The Boneyard
arcs.summary: The finale at the Scales of Judgment, and the choice of who ascends.
beats: Zuni — merged with the Bloodless One and having consumed the corpse of the God of Death, which is why souls cannot pass on — encroaches on the Boneyard as a cosmic horror.
The party fights to the Scales of Judgment, where Zuni is attempting to seize the role of Arbiter.
The Scales are open. Someone must take the seat of power, or the dead roam the world freely forever.
One party member must ascend and become the new Arbiter. They will be a god. They will never return to the Material Plane.
The party decides who among them makes the sacrifice.

antagonists.name: Zuni — The Bloodless One's Herald
antagonists.summary: The court jester who is really Zalazar the Fourteenth, 'The Insane' — a deposed king who has survived thousands of years by changing identity each time a king dies.
points: He has been the current king's jester for this entire reign. Nobody knows his true identity.
Ringleader of a Blood God cult operating within Zalazar for thousands of years.
His right-hand man is embedded in the crown princess's own party as a witch or warlock, fighting beside her while plotting her death.
His lackeys are planted in spectator crowds. The network is vast, patient and invisible.

True goal: the crown princess must die. She carries the Blessing of Radiance, unmanifested in the royal bloodline for 20,000 years and only because she is the first female descendant in that time. She is the only person alive capable of opposing him; the king's sheltered son poses no threat.

antagonists.name: Zalazar the Second — The Radiant
antagonists.summary: Great mage, believed dead ~24,000 years. Became a lich because he looked at what was coming and decided someone had to still be standing when it arrived, even if everyone hated him for it.
points: He has been turning his own people — the original, far vaster Zalazari civilisation to the west — into undead, not to conquer but to preserve them from the Blood God's encroachment. His methods are monstrous; his reasons are not.
He has watched his legacy dismantled, his sacrifice recontextualised as madness, his name become a title without meaning.
He has been losing himself slowly across the millennia, his mind corroding despite the Radiance — and he knows it.
There is no sadness in unlife.

kings.title: The Honored One, The Sun King, The Golden Lion
kings.note: Exemplar. United the Zalazari trolls and led the near-total defeat of the Ogre overlords. An Exemplar like Femur — a detail that raises eyebrows.

kings.title: The Radiant
kings.note: Great mage. Sacrificed his eye. Became the Lich.

kings.title: The Teacher
kings.note: Rewrote all Zalazari history to conceal his forefather's descent into 'madness' — erasing the true purpose of the Eye and the true nature of the Lich.

kings.title: The Warden
kings.note: Not of royal blood. Protector of animals and the weak. Ranger. (Vir'kala)

kings.title: The Crone
kings.note: Not of royal blood. Occult magic. Witch. (Ba'vira)

kings.title: The Humble
kings.note: Not of royal blood. Divine magic. Cleric. (Taz'riya)

kings.title: The Insane
kings.note: Not of royal blood. Psychic. (Zun'hak) — THIS IS ZUNI. Nobody knows.

kings.title: The Indomitable
kings.note: Went to fight on the frontlines many times.

npcs.name: Ti'vola
npcs.role: Royal Emissary, diplomat, messenger

npcs.name: Mu'zala
npcs.role: General of the Zalazari army. Old, stoic, loyal.

npcs.name: Ti'shan
npcs.role: Prodigal warrior from Kilika. Once hotheaded and arrogant; six months of humbling travel later he is calm, grounded and genuinely heroic. Will sacrifice everything for the party before this is over.

npcs.name: Vol'tika
npcs.role: Representative for Kilika, sister to Ti'vola. (32 Diplomacy)

npcs.name: Ma'rimo
npcs.role: Archdruid of Kilika, protector of the forest

npcs.name: Ti'kala
npcs.role: Sister to Ti'shan

npcs.name: Ba'vira
npcs.role: The Swamp Hag. Also known as Zalazar the Twelfth, 'The Crone.'

npcs.name: Wen'kaji
npcs.role: Merchant guild

npcs.name: Amber Hall
npcs.role: Vanguard Commander. Mother of the Alliance's Commander. Rose to the top of the Zalazari military through exceptional ability, navigating a deeply patriarchal system her whole career. Reaches Level 15 by the Vanguard arc. Will die protecting the crown princess.

npcs.name: Jericho Hall
npcs.role: Son of Amber Hall. Vanguard Commander at Forward Camp Amberhall.

npcs.name: Lo'paal
npcs.role: High-ranking administration officer, de facto leader of the Unmasked — manipulated by Zuni, who supplies the masks.

npcs.name: Minor trolls
npcs.role: Ku'dana, Po'goro, Ki'kara, Di'tola, Vol'tola, Ku'taal, He'doro, Ni'kala, Gabrodi, Da'toga, To'rara — general store owner, emissaries, foremen, fishers and so on.

npcs.name: Lukas Brightheart
npcs.role: Skilled craftsman escorted from Port Suna. Survives the Vanguard March.

npcs.name: Mabra Cypherbloom
npcs.role: Met at Woodfall alongside Forward Commander Hall.

npcs.name: Captain Morgan
npcs.role: Alliance general the party once stopped from conquering Zalazar. Goes rogue and joins Zuni with his corrupted fleet.

npcs.name: Jared
npcs.role: Marches with the Vanguard. Dies.

npcs.name: Gazlow
npcs.role: Big Boss of the Undermine. Took the Anvil Fortress as his castle; built the mech powered by the Eye.

npcs.name: Queek
npcs.role: Has struck a bargain with Amber Hall to protect the ratfolk.

npcs.name: Musta the Russari
npcs.role: From the beach resort. Provides his compass to the Mist-cast Morass.

npcs.name: Faunus
npcs.role: Vulpia's father. Merged with the creature he made trying to bring back his wife and daughter; contained by the Feywild's inhabitants.

npcs.name: Aurae
npcs.role: Vulpia's mother. Died in the catastrophic incident where they also lost their daughter.

npcs.name: Dimari-diji
npcs.role: Locked Faunus up to stop the chaotic rift energies leaking further.

npcs.name: The Rat King
npcs.role: A Glimmerling who never came back.

ideas: Femur's tribe was created by the corruption of the Bloodless One. The gift he received from Sarenrae, Goddess of Light and Healing, is what saved him from being as corrupted as his clansmen.
Queek has struck a bargain with Amber Hall to protect the ratfolk.

On the Zalazari trolls: once subjugated by Ogres, Zalazar the First united the troll slaves and cut down almost every last Ogre. Ogres still exist in low numbers, are full citizens, and face no formal discrimination.
Zalazari have remarkably low birth rates, barely replacing their population and not growing meaningfully over millennia — yet their population is vast and steady.
The Queen of the Zalazari is whichever woman conceives a child with the king first.
